# RAG corpus: language rules

## rule: token
kind: lexical

~~~text
token               = IDENT | KEYWORD | UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORD | number | CHAR_LIT
                    | STRING_LIT | OPERATOR | UNSUPPORTED_OP | PUNCT ;
~~~

## rule: IDENT
kind: lexical

~~~text
IDENT               = letter , { letter | digit } ;   (* not a keyword *)
~~~

## rule: letter
kind: lexical

~~~text
letter              = "A".."Z" | "a".."z" | "_" ;
~~~

## rule: digit
kind: lexical

~~~text
digit               = "0".."9" ;
~~~

## rule: KEYWORD
kind: lexical

~~~text
KEYWORD             = "int" | "float" | "double" | "char" | "void" | "if" | "else"
                    | "while" | "for" | "return" | "break" | "continue" ;
~~~

## rule: UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORD
kind: lexical

~~~text
UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORD = "struct" | "union" | "enum" | "typedef" | "switch" | "case"
                    | "default" | "do" | "goto" | "sizeof" | "long" | "short"
                    | "unsigned" | "signed" | "const" | "static" | "extern"
                    | "auto" | "register" | "volatile" ;
~~~

## rule: number
kind: lexical

~~~text
number              = INT_LIT | FLOAT_LIT ;
~~~

## rule: INT_LIT
kind: lexical

~~~text
INT_LIT             = digit , { digit } ;
~~~

## rule: FLOAT_LIT
kind: lexical

~~~text
FLOAT_LIT           = digit , { digit } , "." , digit , { digit } ;
~~~

## rule: CHAR_LIT
kind: lexical

~~~text
CHAR_LIT            = "'" , ( char_char | escape ) , "'" ;   (* exactly one character *)
~~~

## rule: STRING_LIT
kind: lexical

~~~text
STRING_LIT          = '"' , { string_char | escape } , '"' ;  (* may not span lines *)
~~~

## rule: escape
kind: lexical

~~~text
escape              = "\" , ( "n" | "t" | "0" | "'" | '"' | "\" ) ;
~~~

## rule: OPERATOR
kind: lexical

~~~text
OPERATOR            = "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "%" | "=" | "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/="
                    | "%=" | "++" | "--" | "==" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">="
                    | "&&" | "||" | "!" ;
~~~

## rule: UNSUPPORTED_OP
kind: lexical

~~~text
UNSUPPORTED_OP      = "&" | "|" | "^" | "~" | "<<" | ">>" | "->" | "." | "?" | ":" ;
~~~

## rule: PUNCT
kind: lexical

~~~text
PUNCT               = ";" | "," | "(" | ")" | "{" | "}" | "[" | "]" ;
~~~

## rule: directive
kind: lexical

~~~text
directive           = "#" , { any char except newline } ;
~~~

## rule: LINE_COMMENT
kind: lexical

~~~text
LINE_COMMENT        = "//" , { any char except newline } ;
~~~

## rule: BLOCK_COMMENT
kind: lexical

~~~text
BLOCK_COMMENT       = "/*" , { any char } , "*/" ;   (* does not nest *)
~~~

## rule: program
kind: grammar

~~~text
program        = { top_decl } , EOF ;
~~~

## rule: top_decl
kind: grammar

~~~text
top_decl       = type_spec , ( function_def | global_decl ) ;
~~~

## rule: function_def
kind: grammar

~~~text
function_def   = IDENT , "(" , params , ")" , ( block | ";" ) ;
~~~

## rule: params
kind: grammar

~~~text
params         = [ "void" | param_list ] ;
~~~

## rule: param_list
kind: grammar

~~~text
param_list     = param , { "," , param } ;
~~~

## rule: param
kind: grammar

~~~text
param          = type_spec , IDENT ;
~~~

## rule: global_decl
kind: grammar

~~~text
global_decl    = declarator , { "," , declarator } , ";" ;
~~~

## rule: type_spec
kind: grammar

~~~text
type_spec      = "int" | "float" | "double" | "char" | "void" ;
~~~

## rule: declarator
kind: grammar

~~~text
declarator     = IDENT , [ array_suffix ] , [ "=" , expression ] ;
~~~

## rule: array_suffix
kind: grammar

~~~text
array_suffix   = "[" , expression , "]" ;
~~~

## rule: block
kind: grammar

~~~text
block          = "{" , { statement } , "}" ;
~~~

## rule: statement
kind: grammar

~~~text
statement      = var_decl | if_stmt | while_stmt | for_stmt | return_stmt
               | break_stmt | continue_stmt | block | expr_stmt | empty_stmt ;
~~~

## rule: var_decl
kind: grammar

~~~text
var_decl       = var_core , ";" ;
~~~

## rule: var_core
kind: grammar

~~~text
var_core       = type_spec , declarator , { "," , declarator } ;
~~~

## rule: if_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
if_stmt        = "if" , "(" , expression , ")" , statement , [ "else" , statement ] ;
~~~

## rule: while_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
while_stmt     = "while" , "(" , expression , ")" , statement ;
~~~

## rule: for_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
for_stmt       = "for" , "(" , [ for_init ] , ";" , [ expression ] , ";"
               , [ expression ] , ")" , statement ;
~~~

## rule: for_init
kind: grammar

~~~text
for_init       = var_core | expression ;
~~~

## rule: return_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
return_stmt    = "return" , [ expression ] , ";" ;
~~~

## rule: break_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
break_stmt     = "break" , ";" ;
~~~

## rule: continue_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
continue_stmt  = "continue" , ";" ;
~~~

## rule: expr_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
expr_stmt      = expression , ";" ;
~~~

## rule: empty_stmt
kind: grammar

~~~text
empty_stmt     = ";" ;
~~~

## rule: expression
kind: grammar

~~~text
expression     = assignment ;
~~~

## rule: assignment
kind: grammar

~~~text
assignment     = logic_or , [ assign_op , assignment ] ;
~~~

## rule: assign_op
kind: grammar

~~~text
assign_op      = "=" | "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/=" | "%=" ;
~~~

## rule: logic_or
kind: grammar

~~~text
logic_or       = logic_and , { "||" , logic_and } ;
~~~

## rule: logic_and
kind: grammar

~~~text
logic_and      = equality , { "&&" , equality } ;
~~~

## rule: equality
kind: grammar

~~~text
equality       = comparison , { ( "==" | "!=" ) , comparison } ;
~~~

## rule: comparison
kind: grammar

~~~text
comparison     = term , { ( "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ) , term } ;
~~~

## rule: term
kind: grammar

~~~text
term           = factor , { ( "+" | "-" ) , factor } ;
~~~

## rule: factor
kind: grammar

~~~text
factor         = unary , { ( "*" | "/" | "%" ) , unary } ;
~~~

## rule: unary
kind: grammar

~~~text
unary          = ( "!" | "-" | "+" | "++" | "--" ) , unary | postfix ;
~~~

## rule: postfix
kind: grammar

~~~text
postfix        = primary , { "(" , [ arg_list ] , ")" | "[" , expression , "]" }
               , [ "++" | "--" ] ;
~~~

## rule: arg_list
kind: grammar

~~~text
arg_list       = assignment , { "," , assignment } ;
~~~

## rule: primary
kind: grammar

~~~text
primary        = INT_LIT | FLOAT_LIT | CHAR_LIT | STRING_LIT | IDENT
               | "(" , expression , ")" ;
~~~

## rule: sem.declare_before_use
kind: semantic

~~~text
Variables must be declared before use; lookup walks enclosing block scopes,
then file scope. Functions must be declared (prototype or definition) earlier
in the file than any call (C99 rule).

```c
int main(void) {
    y = 3;          /* y was never declared */
    foo(1);         /* foo was never declared */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.unique_in_scope
kind: semantic

~~~text
A name may be declared once per scope; shadowing an outer scope is allowed.
Parameters live in the function body's outermost scope; globals and functions
share file scope. Defining a function body twice is a redeclaration.

```c
int main(void) {
    int x = 1;
    int x = 2;      /* x is already declared in this scope */
    return x;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.function_declarations
kind: semantic

~~~text
A function may have several prototypes and one definition; all must agree on
return type and parameter types.

```c
int f(int a);
float f(int a) {    /* return type disagrees with the prototype */
    return 1.0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.type_compat
kind: semantic

~~~text
Operands, initialisers, assignments, arguments and returns must satisfy
section 3.

```c
int main(void) {
    int x = "hi";       /* a string literal is not an arithmetic value */
    int r = 7.5 % 2;    /* % needs integer operands */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.no_void_values
kind: semantic

~~~text
No variable or parameter may be void; a call to a void function cannot be
used as a value.

```c
void log_it(void) { }
int main(void) {
    int x = log_it();   /* log_it returns no value */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.call_signature
kind: semantic

~~~text
Only functions can be called, with exactly the declared number of arguments,
each convertible to its parameter type.

```c
int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
int main(void) {
    int x = 0;
    x(1);               /* x is not a function */
    return add(1);      /* add expects 2 arguments */
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.return_type
kind: semantic

~~~text
`return expr;` is only allowed in non-void functions and `expr` must convert
to the return type; `return;` only in void functions (stricter than gcc, which
warns).

```c
void f(void) {
    return 5;       /* void function returns a value */
}
int g(void) {
    return;         /* non-void function returns nothing */
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.return_paths
kind: semantic

~~~text
A non-void function other than `main` should return on every path. A
statement returns on every path if it is a `return`, a block in which ANY
statement returns on every path, or an `if` with an `else` whose two branches
both return on every path. Loops never count. Statements that follow a
statement which returns on every path, in the same block, can never run: the
first of them gets WRN-UNREACHABLE-CODE (`sem.unreachable`), not a missing
return. Violation is a warning, as in gcc's -Wreturn-type. `main` implicitly
returns 0.

```c
int f(int b) {
    if (b) {
        return 1;
    }                   /* no return when b is 0 */
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.array_access
kind: semantic

~~~text
An array size must be an integer literal greater than 0 (no variable-length
arrays). Only arrays may be indexed, and the index must have integer type.
Constant out-of-range indices are not checked (runtime behaviour is out of scope).

```c
int main(void) {
    int n = 3;
    int a[n];           /* size must be a literal */
    int x = 1;
    x[0] = 1;           /* x is not an array */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.loop_control
kind: semantic

~~~text
`break` and `continue` may appear only inside `while` or `for`.

```c
int main(void) {
    break;              /* not inside a loop */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.global_init
kind: semantic

~~~text
A global initialiser must be a numeric or char literal, optionally preceded
by `-`.

```c
int x = 4;
int y = x + 1;          /* not a literal */
```
~~~

## rule: sem.builtins
kind: semantic

~~~text
`printf` is declared only if `#include <stdio.h>` appears before its first
use. Its first argument must be a string literal; further arguments may be any
arithmetic values. Format specifiers are not checked. Redeclaring `printf` is a
redeclaration.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) {
    int x = 1;
    printf(x);          /* first argument must be a string literal */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.conditions
kind: semantic

~~~text
Conditions of `if`, `while` and `for` must be arithmetic (any non-zero value
is true). A plain `=` as the outermost operator of a condition produces a
warning, as in gcc's -Wparentheses.

```c
int main(void) {
    int x = 0;
    if (x = 5) {        /* assignment, probably meant == */
        x = 1;
    }
    return x;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.entry_point
kind: semantic

~~~text
The program must define `int main()` or `int main(void)`. Real C reports a
missing main at link time; this compiler reports it at the end of semantic
analysis.

```c
void g(void) { }        /* the file has no main */
```
~~~

## rule: sem.unused_declaration
kind: semantic

~~~text
A local variable that is declared but never read produces a warning.
Assigning with `=` is not a read. Compound assignment (`+=` and the like) and
`++`/`--` both read and write. Parameters and globals are exempt.

```c
int main(void) {
    int t = 1;          /* t is never read */
    return 0;
}
```
~~~

## rule: sem.unreachable
kind: semantic

~~~text
The first statement after a `break`, a `continue`, or any statement that
returns on every path (a `return`, a block containing one, or an `if`/`else`
whose branches both return on every path; see `sem.return_paths`) in the same
block produces one warning. This is a teaching warning that gcc does not emit.

```c
int main(void) {
    return 0;
    return 1;           /* can never run */
}
```
~~~
